zen.text: Zendikar is a wild plane where the Roil redraws the world as it passes and only the hedrons stay unchanged.

Its past is already full of loss: the ancient kor empire fell to rebellions, civil wars and the Eldrazi, and the angels who tried to resist the first stirring of the Eldrazi were defeated and now wear their halos over their eyes.
Nahiri built a network of hedrons over forty years to imprison the Eldrazi, guided by Ugin, while Ob Nixilis, his spark lost, plotted revenge on the plane.

wwk.text: In Worldwake, Zendikar's ancient forces begin to awaken, and the world starts to wreak havoc on the people living on it.
Sabra joins her first expedition out of the Murasa Expedition House, hired to find a chest, but Anowon ambushes her and slits her throat; she survives and returns to tell her employer what happened.

roe.text: Zendikar learns in Rise of the Eldrazi that the horrors it had trapped long ago are loose again, and the world itself seems to have turned against adventurers.

Thousands of years earlier three Eldrazi had descended on Zendikar, and Ugin, Nahiri and Sorin Markov chose Nahiri's world for its lush ecosystems and dynamic mana, with Sorin luring the Eldrazi, Ugin binding them with colorless magic and Nahiri building the hedron network that formed their prison.
Once Nissa Revane shattered the main hedron, the titans were released, the hedrons coalesced into colossal Eldrazi superstructures, and Zendikar's brood lineages sprang up around the three titans.

The angels who stood against the Eldrazi were cut down and left with halos worn down over their eyes, and the merfolk came to see that their gods Cosi and Ula were only dim memories of Kozilek and Ulamog.

m11.text: On Zendikar the Eldrazi arise once more, and the merfolk come to understand that they had mistaken the Eldrazi names for the legends of gods.
The Eldrazi never introduced themselves, since their consciousness is too alien for the Zendikari's language to latch onto.

cns.text: Zendikar is shown through Nissa's eyes after the Eldrazi swarm and Ulamog's return devastate her Joraga tribe, and she wakes pinned under a fallen tree, too drained to planeswalk.
A human man pulls her free and heals her as Ulamog closes in, and she later joins Hamadi, Bahkut, Alira and the kor twins Khali and Sha'heel on a climb through gravity fields of floating boulders.
When a Pathrazer spawn of Ulamog attacks the party, Khali and Sha'heel snare it with ropes while Nissa pours her power into earth elementals that crush it.
Afterward Hamadi tells Nissa that Zendikar has chosen her and that Shaya means Worldwaker.

m15.text: Zendikar's hedrons were arranged by Ugin to direct leylines of energy across the plane.
Deep underground, Ob Nixilis rotates hedrons on the cavern walls and tests their runes, hating Zendikar because Nahiri bound a hedron into him that took his power and his wings.
He studies the hedrons for centuries and lures planeswalkers, and with Bala Ged's destruction he feels his spark within reach.
Meanwhile Ulamog's brood attacks the Joraga and Nissa barely survives as their only survivor, saved by Hamadi's band.

ori.text: Zendikar is in pain in Magic Origins, and as the Eldrazi stir, Nahiri wakes from her long slumber, visits the hedron network's sites, buries the Eldrazi broods she finds, and decides she must stop them alone.
Nissa, whose people had angered the land and faced its wrath, connects with Zendikar's soul and learns from Mazik that Zendikar isn't after her but needs her help.
She realizes the Roil is Zendikar's fear of the dark knot and calms the land by humming her mother's animist song, then later understands she was never chosen or alone but one with Zendikar.
Elsewhere Gideon holds a canyon pass against Eldrazi spawn so survivors from the destroyed Bala Ged can escape, and learns from Munda that a great host of Eldrazi descends on Sea Gate.

bfz.text: In Battle for Zendikar the plane is overrun, with Sea Gate, Sejiri and Bala Ged falling to the Eldrazi, as Nissa, who had released the titans thinking they would leave, wakes unable to feel Zendikar or Ashaya.
Jace learns that Ulamog is drawn to concentrations of population, so that Sea Gate and other refuges will become tombs, and he alters Jori's mind so she will carry the warning to Gideon.

Kiora drives Eldrazi off a hundred merfolk refugees and heads for Sea Gate to stop Ulamog, while Gideon takes the lead of the planeswalkers facing the Eldrazi and Ob Nixilis siphons the hedron network at Tazeem and awakens Kozilek.
Nissa, realizing she is neither her old self nor her controlled self, pours her essence into Khalni Heart, and Zendikar's soul returns to the land.

ogw.text: Zendikar becomes the battlefield of the Gatewatch in Oath of the Gatewatch, when Chandra arrives, frees Gideon, Jace and Nissa from Ob Nixilis and scares the demon off the plane.
The four swear an oath to stand together, forming the Gatewatch, while Jace and Nissa devise a plan to destroy the titans permanently, breaking Jace's promise to Ugin.
Gideon and Nissa carve a path through the Eldrazi swarm, and Chandra channels her flame through Zendikar's ley lines to incinerate Ulamog and Kozilek in Zendikar's Last Stand.
Ugin berates Jace and his friends for killing the ancient creatures, and Jace and Gideon resolve to leave Zendikar to gather intelligence while Nissa stays as its guardian.

znr.text: Zendikar is Nahiri's world in Zendikar Rising, and she returns determined to rid it of the Roil, which did not stop even after the Eldrazi died.
Nissa also returns, and when adventurers awaken the Emeria Skyclave and the other six, the ruins rise back into the sky with their defenses awake.
Nahiri uses the Lithoform Core despite Nissa's warnings, killing Zareth and pushing Akiri off the ruin, and her disregard for Zendikar's soul turns Nissa against her.
Nissa prevails and uses the Core to heal Zendikar and restore its wild nature, and Nahiri swears revenge on Jace.

mat.text: In The Aftermath, Zendikar is Nahiri's home plane, and she finds it wrecked by Phyrexia and concedes that this was her fault.
Uncompleated and desparked, she tries to remove the metal from the Skyclave but lacks the power to restore the land, and she vows that no planeswalker will set foot on Zendikar again.

fdn.text: Zendikar's Roil does not stop after the Eldrazi die, though in theory their death should have stilled it.
